intended_object: The inclusion map {0, 1} ↪ [0, 1], i.e. the boundary ∂I of the unit interval included into I, as a continuous map. This comes from the name and from the companion definition `zeroOne := {0, 1} : Set ℝ`.
explanation: The map sends a point x of {0, 1}, viewed as a subset of ℝ, to the same real number x, now as an element of I = [0, 1]. The proof that x lies in [0, 1] only checks the two cases x = 0 and x = 1. Continuity comes from `fun_prop`. So this is exactly the inclusion of the subspace {0, 1} into [0, 1], which is a specific map and not a general construction. Generalizing it would not make sense, so it is not too narrow. I found no Mathlib declaration that bundles this exact map; the closest generic tool is `Set.inclusion` between subsets of ℝ. The definition is correct.
